title: Grace = 1 sound in English… 4 in Korean?! Comment your name 👇 #learnkorean
caption:
Grace → 그레이스 (geu·re·i·seu)
More: Mark → 마크 (ma·keu) · James → 제임스 (je·im·seu)

Korean writes names by how they sound, not by spelling — sounds like the g in "gr-" and the final s get their own block (그 · 스), so a one-syllable name becomes four blocks. (These follow the official Korean spelling for foreign names.)

✍️ Comment just your first name 👇 I'll reply with it in Hangul for the first 3 days.
(First name only, please — no full names or personal info.)

alt: Top-down view of a wooden desk. Under a caption COMMENT YOUR NAME 👇 / I'll write it in Korean, a speech bubble says Grace and a black marker writes it in Korean on a red HELLO my name is sticker, one block at a time: 그 · 레 · 이 · 스. As each block is finished a voice reads it, a number 1 to 4 pops above it and its sound appears under it (geu re i seu). A voice says 그레이스!, then One sound in English. Four in Korean! while pills say 1 sound in English → 4 in Korean! and the four blocks bounce. Finally a blank sticker gets a question mark, the bubble says Your name, and pills say Comment your name 👇 / I'll write it in Korean ✍️.
